title: Ollie's rather forgetful road trip
intro: Fancy hearing my story, mate? Australia, New York, and a rather unreliable memory. Help me find nine missing words. I have a little souvenir for you.
wrong: Not quite, mate. Have another think. I have left you a little clue.

questions.narrative: I grew up in Australia. One day I packed my ... darn it! What do you call the bag you wear on your back?
questions.hint: You carry it on your back, with two straps.
questions.reply: Ah yes, backpack! I'm getting old, mate. Anyway, I was on my way to New York. Absolutely terrified. Mostly of the airport coffee.

questions.narrative: Before I left, a ... oh, what's that Australian animal that hops on two big feet? It was watching me pack. Very judgemental.
questions.hint: It hops and carries its baby in a pouch.
questions.reply: A kangaroo! That's the one. It had better legs than me, but no passport. So I went to the airport on my own.

questions.narrative: I crossed the Pacific in a ... darn it, the thing with wings! Not a bird. It has seats and tiny bags of peanuts.
questions.hint: It takes off from an airport and carries many passengers.
questions.reply: A plane, of course! Many hours later, New York appeared below us. So many lights! I thought somebody had left every oven on.

questions.narrative: My first stop was the Statue of ... oh, what was her name? The big green lady holding a torch. Lovely hat. Terrible place to lose your keys.
questions.hint: Her name is another English word for freedom.
questions.reply: Liberty! That's it. I tried waving. She didn't wave back. Fair enough, her arms must get tired.

questions.narrative: Then I visited the ... State Building. Darn it! I remember the lifts, but not the name. That famous skyscraper in Manhattan.
questions.hint: Think of the Empire State Building.
questions.reply: Empire! Up I went. The view was brilliant. My knees were less enthusiastic. I bought you a little souvenir on the way down.

questions.narrative: Next I wandered into Central ... darn it! The big green place in Manhattan, with trees and lakes. Lovely spot for a rest.
questions.hint: A green place where people walk, play and enjoy nature.
questions.reply: Park! Central Park. I tried jogging for twelve seconds. Even the squirrels looked disappointed.

questions.narrative: Then I walked across the Brooklyn ... oh, what do you call the thing over the East River? It connects Manhattan and Brooklyn.
questions.hint: You can walk across it above the water.
questions.reply: Bridge! Brooklyn Bridge. I took forty photos. Thirty-nine were of my thumb. The other one was rather good.

questions.narrative: After that, I found Times ... darn it! That busy city space with all the bright lights and enormous screens. What a place!
questions.hint: A city space surrounded by buildings. Its name is also a shape with four equal sides.
questions.reply: Square! Times Square. I nearly bought sunglasses at night. Then I checked that your souvenir was still in my bag.

questions.narrative: I put the souvenir in my ... oh no, not again! That bag with two straps. What did we call it at the start?
questions.hint: It is the same word as the first gap.
questions.reply: Backpack! You're a lifesaver, mate. Here's your little New York souvenir. And fifty coins and eighty XP for putting up with my memory. Cheers!
